document_check.note: Document is Zhang S, Yin Q, Zheng Y et al., 'Cortical structure of left superior parietal cortex is associated with cognition and dual tasking: A cross-sectional preliminary study between mild cognitive impairment and healthy controls', Behavioural Brain Research 479 (2025) 115360. Cross-sectional, 30 MCI vs 30 healthy controls; Table 3 reports single-task TUG not different (p=0.64) and dual-task TUG and dual-task cost different (p=0.012, p=0.014), which is the result the review cites.

cited_result: Between-group comparison at one time point: dual-task Timed Up and Go time (HC 24.92±4.42 s vs MCI 29.23±8.02 s, p=0.012) and dual-task cost (0.45±0.35 vs 0.70±0.42, p=0.014) differed between 30 MCI and 30 healthy controls, whereas single-task TUG time did not (17.60±2.89 vs 17.29±2.34 s, p=0.64).
tool_reason: The cited result is a comparison of a performance measure between MCI and control groups measured at a single time point in a cross-sectional design.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined
domains.rationale: Age range, MCI criteria, control MMSE/MoCA cut-offs and exclusion criteria are all stated.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: The inclusion criteria of MCI group refers to the core clinical diagnostic criteria previously released [33]: (1) cognitive impairment reported by patients or informed persons, or expert physicians; (2) the presence of objective evidence for impairment in one or more cognitive domains

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: Setting (hospital outpatient unit and community, Guangzhou), recruitment period and group demographics are reported; the sampling method (consecutive or convenience) is not stated, and the sample is predominantly female.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: Participants were recruited from outpatient unit in hospital and community from October 2021 to September 2022.

signalling.question: Were participant characteristics reported by group?
signalling.quote: We enrolled 30 participants in both HC and MCI group (male/female: 7/23; 4/26). There were no significant difference between age, body mass index, and years of education between the MCI group and HC group (p>0.05; Table 1).

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure (MCI group membership) measured in a valid and reliable way
domains.rationale: Group status was assigned by experienced clinicians using a standard cognitive battery (MMSE, CDR, MoCA and others).

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: All subjects were assessed by medical doctors and physical therapists with at least three years of work experience.

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: MCI follows published core clinical criteria with a CDR ceiling; controls meet education-adjusted MMSE and MoCA cut-offs. No numeric threshold for 'objective impairment' is given for MCI, a minor gap.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: (4) the diagnosis of dementia has not been satisfied (with Clinical Dementia Rating Scale (CDR) up to 0.5

signalling.question: Were control criteria objective?
signalling.quote: for illiterate individuals ≥20 points, for those with elementary school education ≥23 points, and for others ≥27 points

domains.rationale: Age, gender, education and BMI are named as covariates and compared between groups.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: Covariates included age, gender, years of education and body mass index.

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated
domains.rationale: The cited TUG comparisons are unadjusted independent t-tests; groups were not matched, and covariates were applied only to the within-group partial correlations and the cortical vertex analysis. Reliance on non-significant baseline tests in 60 participants (education 11.53 vs 10.13 years, p=0.097; age 58.1 vs 60.5 years) is not a strategy.

signalling.question: Was the cited between-group comparison adjusted or the groups matched?
signalling.quote: The data was tested with independent sample t-test and expressed as the mean ± standard deviation (x±s) when the data was normally distributed.

signalling.question: Were the named covariates applied to the cited result?
signalling.quote: we further performed partial Spearman correlation analysis within each group to explore the relationships between cortical thickness and surface area, and performance of the TUG tests (including single and dual-task conditions, the DTC), along with performance of the cognitive tests. Covariates included age, gender, years of education and body mass index.

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way
domains.rationale: The TUG used is a modified version (10 m walk to a table, retrieving and dialling a phone); the number of recorded trials, timing method, reliability of this variant and whether assessors were blind to group are not reported. Test order was randomised.

signalling.question: Was the outcome measure valid and applied in a standard way?
signalling.quote: Under the single-task condition, individuals were asked to rise from a chair, walk at a comfortable pace to a table ten meters away, retrieve a cellphone, return to the chair, and sit down.

signalling.question: Were reliability, number of recorded trials and assessor blinding reported?
signalling.quote: Searched for test-retest reliability of the modified TUG, number of timed trials, timing device and blinding of assessors to group; only practice trials are described: 'Each participant completed one practice trial for both the single-task and dual-task TUG test (ST-TUG and DT-TUG)'

signalling.question: Were order effects addressed?
signalling.quote: The order of the cognitive assessments, the TUG tests and MRI scans was randomized to minimize potential biases.

domains.rationale: Normality-guided t-tests are appropriate for a two-group continuous comparison, and a power calculation was made for DT-TUG. The 'separates where single-task does not' contrast is supported by the formal DTC test rather than only by significance versus non-significance.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: There was no significant difference in the execution time of single-task TUG test between the MCI and HC groups (p> 0.05), while a significant difference in the execution time of the dual-task paradigm was observed (T= −2.58, p= 0.012). The DTC was also increased in MCI group (T= −2.55, p= 0.014; Table 3).

signalling.question: Was the sample size justified for this outcome?
signalling.quote: a total sample size of 29 participants per group was calculated with a type I error of 5 % and a statistical power of 75 %.

overall: High risk of bias (JBI analytical cross-sectional: item 6, confounder strategy, answered No; item 7 unclear)
overall_rationale: Under this review's rule a 'No' on the confounder-strategy item gives high risk. The cited dual-task and single-task TUG group differences are crude t-tests with no matching or adjustment for age, sex, education or BMI, in a small convenience-type sample. The modified TUG's reliability, number of recorded trials and assessor blinding are also unreported. Inclusion criteria, case definition and the analysis are otherwise adequate.
